solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Officer coming across a fine hole in one exposed seam

indicators.note: the officer's abbreviation lies across, straddling, the single letter that follows

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
in golf a hole in one is an ace

explanation.surface: An officer finds a fine hole-in-one on a golf course where a seam of rock lies exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a mine where the coal seam is laid bare and worked is exactly an exposed seam.

clue.text: Firm initially monitors scheme to import island's beef

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of monitors
the scheme takes the island inside it

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A company watches over a plan to bring in an island's beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' is not meat but slang for a grievance, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for to grumble or protest.

clue.text: World book finally abridged

indicators.note: shortened by its final letter

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: A world book is at last cut down to size.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound volume of maps of the world.

clue.text: Boxing manager's leisure time left creditor furious

parts.note: leisure time is fun
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: a furious creditor is in a state, so his letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A boxing manager's time off has left a creditor fuming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' suggests the ring; this manager deals in coffins.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker manages the boxing up of the dead in coffins, a witty cryptic description.

clue.text: Fifty fail to appear in entire contest

indicators.note: the fifty is absent from the word for entire

parts.note: complete means entire
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty competitors fail to turn up for the whole contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to vie or take part, and contest as a verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Find vessel inside, set back

indicators.note: the vessel is placed inside the other piece
back means the word for set is read backwards

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a vessel indoors and has to put it back.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up something is to discover or find it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Simple duties can, when mixed with this absorbing work

indicators.note: the letters of all these words are blended together
the word this takes in the work, adding its letters to the pool being mixed

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Simple duties can be mixed with this engrossing work.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsophisticated means naive and plain, a synonym for simple.

clue.text: One hates dragging on small donkey in middle of fun run

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the central letters
the centre of the phrase is its middle two letters

parts.note: moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone drags a small donkey along during a charity fun run.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken together, fun run's middle pair is NR. 'dragging' means puffing on a cigarette, not pulling a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonsmoker dislikes taking drags on cigarettes, a playful description.

clue.text: Like green areas in gym

indicators.note: the meadows go inside the gym lesson

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym
leas are meadows, green areas

explanation.surface: Green spaces are set inside a gym, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' reads as a preposition; it is the verb, as in 'do as you like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Do as you please means do as you wish, so the verb matches like.

clue.text: Philby stops one like him revealing a lot

indicators.note: the name plugs, or stops up, the middle of the other word

parts.note: Philby was a spy, so one like him is a spy
Kim Philby was the British double agent who spied for the Soviets

explanation.surface: Kim Philby halts a fellow spy who gives too much away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealing a lot' suggests spilling secrets; here it describes scanty clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy clothing is scanty, so it shows plenty of skin.

clue.text: Irish sea area, run down, gallons escaping

indicators.note: the gallons get away, leaving the word for run down

parts.note: to run someone down is to malign them

explanation.surface: A ship is run down in an Irish sea area, with fuel leaking away.
explanation.walkthrough: MALIN is one of the shipping forecast areas read out by the BBC, off the north coast of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Malin is the shipping-forecast zone named after Malin Head, Ireland's northernmost point.

clue.text: Be reasonable as men seek to be redeployed

indicators.note: redeploying the troops rearranges these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Common sense, says a commander, as his men look to be posted elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To make sense is to be logical or reasonable, an idiomatic equivalent.

clue.text: Large sea bream tormented ray

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: a tormented fish is twisted about, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A big sea bream is tormented by a ray, apparently a fishy quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' looks like another fish beside the bream, but it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A focused beam of coherent light is a kind of ray.

clue.text: Grills fruits at Halloween, excluding family

indicators.note: leaving out the family from the Halloween fruits

parts.note: pumpkins are the fruits carved into lanterns at Halloween
kin means family

explanation.surface: Someone grills Halloween pumpkins but leaves the family out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grills' pretends to be cooking; it means questions closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone for information is to grill or interrogate them.

clue.text: One million beans perhaps creating sudden urge

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
beans are an example of pulses

explanation.surface: A million beans might give someone a sudden craving.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a spur-of-the-moment desire to act, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Psychic here taking in Channel Islands

indicators.note: the word for here absorbs the abbreviation

parts.note: to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: A psychic here is visiting the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescient means having foreknowledge, which a psychic claims.

clue.text: Old friend of Hamlet ignoring King's hunting call

indicators.note: the king is passed over, so his letter is dropped

parts.note: Yorick is the jester Hamlet remembers ('Alas, poor Yorick'); with the clue's possessive he becomes Yorick's
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for King

explanation.surface: Yorick, old friend of Hamlet, ignores the King's hunting call.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on King's does double work: read as the possessive it makes Yorick's, from which R is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoicks is the traditional cry of foxhunters urging on the hounds.

clue.text: Steer game where Blues won

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A steer plays a game where the Blues won.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is a sporting award given at Oxford and Cambridge, the pair known together as Oxbridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportsmen at Oxford and Cambridge universities win Blues for representing them.

clue.text: One saying "No" does perhaps encapsulate part of UK

indicators.note: the animals enclose the abbreviation within them

parts.note: does, female deer, are an example of deer
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Someone saying no perhaps does wrap up a region of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' reads as a verb; it is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: A denier is a person who refuses or rejects a claim.

clue.text: Begrudge gift, heading off

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, is taken away

parts.note: a present is a gift

explanation.surface: Someone begrudges a gift and heads off.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent is to feel bitter about something, much like to begrudge it.

clue.text: Disease in granny's heart and chest, lacking oxygen

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters
the chest goes without its oxygen

parts.note: the thorax is the chest
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An illness strikes granny's heart and chest, starving her of oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthrax is a serious bacterial infection of livestock and people.

clue.text: Retailer only stocks flight controller

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer in its letters, as a shop stocks goods

explanation.surface: Only one retailer sells the flight controller.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged flap on a wing that controls an aircraft's roll.

clue.text: Horseman spots revolutionary engaging our lot

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the pronoun inside it
turning round, so the word for spots is read backwards

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots
us means our lot

explanation.surface: A horseman spots a revolutionary engaging with our group.
explanation.definitionFit: A hussar is a light cavalry soldier, a mounted fighter.

clue.text: Moneylender, ambiguous, dumping first of accounts receivable

indicators.note: getting rid of the initials from the end of the word for ambiguous

parts.note: something ambiguous is unclear

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: An unclear lender dumps the start of his accounts receivable.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, who lends money against pledges.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang has long called a pawnbroker 'uncle', a lender of cash on pawned goods.

clue.text: Legal advisor, hence authorised to meet troops

parts.note: so means therefore, hence
licit means lawful, authorised
OR is Other Ranks, ordinary troops

explanation.surface: A legal advisor is therefore cleared to meet soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor is a British lawyer who advises clients directly.

clue.text: Beat disease suffocating lion losing energy

indicators.note: the disease wraps around the other piece

parts.note: TB is tuberculosis

indicators.note: the lion drops the energy

parts.note: a lion is a celebrated person, a hero
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A disease smothers a lion that has run out of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a pulse or rhythmic beat.

clue.text: Bribe Society with tiny note, half-heartedly

parts.note: wee means tiny

indicators.note: the doubled letters at the heart of the note lose one of the pair

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: A society offers a bribe with a tiny banknote, without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is the British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement, money or a favour given to win compliance.

clue.text: Did exhaust part for American's car by day

parts.note: tire is the American spelling of tyre, a part of a car

explanation.surface: An exhaust part for an American's car is fitted by the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' looks like a car part beside the tire, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To have tired someone is to have worn them out, so it did exhaust them.

clue.text: Still dealing with infringement

parts.note: re means concerning, dealing with
a tort is a civil wrong, an infringement of rights

explanation.surface: Someone is still dealing with a breach of the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' is not the adverb but the noun: distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a glass vessel used in distillation, a kind of still.

clue.text: Hard to believe doing without credit, hard to swallow

indicators.note: the credit is removed from the longer word

parts.note: incredible means hard to believe
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Something unbelievable without credit is also unpalatable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard to swallow' looks like a repeat of 'hard to believe', but it is meant literally: not fit to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Inedible food cannot be eaten, literally too hard to get down.
